title: Composite checkpoint crash consistency and issuance reconciliation

preserved_failure_lineage.summary: The reconciliation schema was not initialized before the composite journal attempted its first reconciliation digest. All Pilot 8 cases errored in fixture setup before scientific assertions.
The clean CURRENT promotion used cumulative sqlite3.Connection.total_changes instead of the affected-row count of the exact conditional UPDATE, causing false-denial of clean issuance.
Only the preregistered narrow row-accounting mechanism repair was applied; no endpoint, expected outcome, binding rule, generation rule, or authority boundary was relaxed.

supported_claim: On the tested same-host SQLite prototype, a platform-owned HMAC-authenticated durable composite-checkpoint journal with explicit PENDING/CURRENT state, exact permit-ledger and reconciliation-ledger digest binding, permit-authority epoch binding, monotonic generation, issuance identity, and authenticated predecessor chaining failed closed across the preregistered simulated crash boundaries, stale-state recovery attempts, semantic issuance rebinding, predecessor/authentication tampering, trusted-minimum rollback, latest-checkpoint deletion, and same-generation concurrency conflicts. An exact matching authenticated PENDING issuance could be reconciled to CURRENT exactly once, post-CURRENT response-loss replay returned the same durable checkpoint, and clean higher-generation issuance remained live.
not_proven: Abrupt operating-system process death or SIGKILL semantics; Pilot 8 crash points are simulated exceptions around committed SQLite transitions
Separate-process isolation of the composite checkpoint signing authority or key
Atomic commitment across independent storage systems
Atomic commitment to an external KMS, HSM, or checkpoint service
Protection after compromise of both the durable journal and the composite authentication key or trusted-minimum authority
next_falsification_target: EXP-I Pilot 9: abrupt subprocess termination around composite checkpoint issuance and recovery. Replace simulated exception crash points with parent-observed child-process readiness plus external process termination, then reopen durable state from a fresh process and test fail-closed recovery, idempotent replay, same-generation conflict prevention, and positive liveness.
